answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce bond before earning fees or voting. Every identity needs its own anchor of capital, so splitting one operator into many accounts multiplies funds tied up without multiplying resources. Proven fraud burns the bond; honest agents reclaim it after a delay. This makes fake identities costly at scale: an attacker must immobilize real capital and risk losing it, rather than minting names freely in a harbor. Even reaching the ledge of participation requires that expense.
